title: Silica Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Silica"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

title: Orthophosphate (P) Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Orthophosphate (P)"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)

gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

title: Nitrogen- Total Kjeldahl Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Nitrogen- Total Kjeldahl"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

title: Nitrate-Nitrite (N) Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Nitrate-Nitrite (N)"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")

})

title: Chlorophyll a Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Chlorophyll a"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Ammonia (N)"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

title: FCRWQDC SEACAR Analysis
text:
This project: 1. compares SEACAR standard exports to an aggregated dataset developed in previous years 2. generates rate of change analyses for each water quality parameter 3. creates a dashboardDataSEACAR.csv from the SEACAR standard export for use in the FCRWQDC Data Visualization Tool

Upstream Data
The following data sources should be downloaded and placed in ./data/: 1. Unified_WQ_Database\(2023\ updated\).csv from SEACAR standard export page. 2. previous year’s dashboardData.csv from this gdrive folder produced by USF-IMARS/FCRWQDC_data_ingest

title: Ammonium (N) Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Ammonium (N)"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

title: Nitrate (N) Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Nitrate (N)"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

title: Nitrite (N) Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Nitrite (N)"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

title: Nitrogen- Total Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Nitrogen- Total"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

title: Phosphorus- Total Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Phosphorus- Total"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})

  gt_tbl <- color_column(

title: Turbidity Rate of Change Analysis
text:
A rate of change is calculated for each station using a seasonal Mann Kendall slope calculation.


get data for params$batch_value
source(here::here(glue::glue("{params$batch_name}/getData.R")))

df <- getData(params$batch_value)


[1] "getting data for Turbidity"




create station statistics dataframe
library(here)
library(lubridate)  # for mdy_hms()
library(pander)  # for display
library(dplyr)  # for %>%
source(here("R/seasonalMannKendall.R"))

# create table of samples for each station
samples_df <- df %>%
  # construct datetime column from Month,Day,Year
  mutate(datetime = ymd(paste(Year, Month, Day))) %>%
  # drop any with empty required columns
  filter(!is.na(Site) & !is.na(datetime) & !is.na(Value)) %>%
  # parse the "YYYY-MM-DD" strings into POSIXct
  distinct()  # drop duplicate rows


# add statistics for each station
sample_stats_df <- samples_df %>%
  group_by(Source, Site) %>%
  reframe(
    {
      tmp <- seasonalMannKendall(
        datetime,
        Value
      )
    },
    n_values = n(),
    mean = mean(Value),
    min = min(Value),
    max = max(Value),
    coefficient.of.variation = sd(Value) / mean(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # create column significant_slope
    significant_slope = ifelse(z <= 0.05, slope, NA_real_),
    pvalue = z
  ) %>%
  # drop unwanted columns added by seasonalMannKendall
  select(
    -z,
    -tau,
    -chi_square
  )

# print(head(sample_stats_df))
# # display sample_stats_df with pander
# pander(sample_stats_df)




save stats to csv
dataDir <- here("data", "exports", params$batch_name)

# create dir if does not exist
if (!dir.exists(dataDir)) {
  dir.create(dataDir)
}

# save file
sample_stats_df %>%
  write.csv(paste0(dataDir, "/", params$batch_value, ".csv"))




display with gt
library(gt)
library(scales)
library(tidyselect)  # for all_of()
library(RColorBrewer) # for brewer.pal()

# ── color_column() ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gt_tbl   : a gt object that you’ve already created (e.g. `sample_stats_df %>% gt()`)
# df       : the original data.frame (must contain the column you want to color)
# column   : a string, e.g. "slope" or "n_values"
# palette  : a character vector of colours to feed to col_numeric()
#
color_column <- function(gt_tbl, df, column, 
                         palette = c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet"),
                         domain = NULL) {
  # 1) Pull out that column’s numeric values
  vals <- df[[column]]
  if (!is.numeric(vals)) {
    stop(sprintf("`%s` is not numeric; data_color() requires a numeric column.", column))
  }
  
  # 2) Compute its min and max (ignoring NA)
  min_val <- min(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.null(domain)) {
    domain <- c(min_val, max_val)
  }
  
  # 3) Call data_color() on the gt table for that single column
  gt_tbl %>%
    data_color(
      columns = all_of(column),
      colors  = col_numeric(
        palette = palette,
        domain  = domain
      )
    )
}
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# 1) First build your gt table as usual:
gt_tbl <- sample_stats_df %>% 
  gt()

# slope blue (-) to red (+) (0 centered)
tryCatch({
  min_slope <- min(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_slope <- max(sample_stats_df$slope,  na.rm = TRUE)
  max_abs_slope <- max(abs(min_slope), abs(max_slope))
  gt_tbl <- color_column(
    gt_tbl, 
    df     = sample_stats_df, 
    column = "slope",
    palette = rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")),
    domain  = c(-max_abs_slope, max_abs_slope)
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  print("Error in slope color column")
  print(e)
})
